node-1.label: Painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis for 1 month

node-2.label: Patient is a 78-year-old man with medical history of elevated white blood cell count and inguinal lymphadenopathy discovered 9 years prior; 4 years after initial presentation he experienced fatigue, weight loss, and loss of appetite.

node-3.label: Current illness began 1 month before admission with asymptomatic 'green-yellow welts' and swelling of the glans penis; the swelling became progressively painful and reached the size of an 'orange' over 4 days.

node-4.label: Previous treatments with topical antibiotics, antifungal agents, hydrogen peroxide soaks, warm compresses, and cephalexin showed no improvement.

node-5.label: Physical examination showed the patient appeared healthy; glans penis and corona were grossly edematous, with a 3.7 × 3.3-cm tender, firm ulcer on the ventral surface of the penis with overlying black eschar, adherent yellow crust, and granulation tissue; no urethral discharge was present.

why.why: The pathologist and radiologist analyses confirm that the clonal CD20+/CD79a+/CD5+ B lymphocytes with IgH rearrangement are definitive for B-cell lymphoma, and PET-avid abdominal/peripancreatic nodes establish systemic involvement. Negative cultures, normal labs, and failed antimicrobial therapy exclude infection. This supports penile malignancy/hematologic neoplasia with near-certainty, raising confidence from 0.95 to 0.97.

Expert analyses state that negative cultures, normal routine labs, and antimicrobial failure effectively exclude infectious etiologies, while the biopsy-proven clonal B-cell lymphoproliferative disorder with systemic PET-avid nodes is definitive. This further reduces the already low probability of atypical/necrotizing infection from 0.05 to 0.01.

The pathologist confirms that the clonal IgH rearrangement and CD20/CD79a/CD5 immunophenotype are definitive for B-cell lymphoma, effectively excluding a reactive inflammatory/autoimmune ulcer. The radiologist's concurrence, along with negative cultures and failed antimicrobial therapy, supports this and lowers confidence from 0.02 to 0.01.

Expert analyses explicitly exclude sexually transmitted infection in light of biopsy-confirmed B-cell lymphoma and systemic PET findings, supported by negative cultures and failed antimicrobial therapy. Confidence remains at 0.01, effectively ruled out.
